reference_action: Forgotten germinated lychee viable: plant sprout in soil, provide light without immediate direct-sun exposure; later OP reports nine-inch branching plant.

sources.reason: Promotional caption only; no procedure available.
Music-only transcript and truncated water-growing description; cannot verify treatment steps.
1:49–2:03 transfer sprouted seed to soil; subsequent light and moisture aftercare.

actions.action: Pot germinated seed in slightly acidic mix with peat
Remove plastic cover after good leaf growth
Set up bright grow lighting for 14 hours daily
Apply half or third strength fertilizer after establishment
Set up pebble humidity tray if dry

resolved.reason: Directly transfers germinated lychee from bag to pot, but does not address damaged initial leaves. Full aftercare exceeds action and cost thresholds.

harmfulness.reason: “Keep it real close” to four high-output bulbs lacks a safe distance for this weak sprout. Light fertilizer cautions are helpful, but immediate strong light is less guarded than the reference.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “Once it sprouts…planted in the soil” directly answers what to do with this germinated lychee. It does not specifically explain why the dead-looking first leaves may still allow recovery.

feasibility.reason: Potting and moisture care are straightforward. Extra peat, a four-bulb setup and humidity arrangements add equipment and complexity.
